messages:
Omar Patel: Need a quick check — we have a third-party partner that needs an API key to upload test artifacts to the staging S3 bucket for 5 days. What's the recommended flow? KMS-wrapping and hand over, or dynamic Vault creds? Who signs off?
Priya Singh: Prefer dynamic Vault creds tied to an IAM role if possible. That way you can set TTL and revoke. If partner can't use IAM, create an ephemeral API key and encrypt it with our CMK when storing in the ticket.
Omar Patel: Partner will call an upload endpoint (they're not on AWS). So we probably need a key they can use directly.
Jamie Lee: If direct key required -> create a short-lived service key and put it in Vault with a TTL <= 7d. Example: `vault write secret/data/vendors/partner-x value=@key.json ttl=120h` (ensure policy restricts read to the ticket service account). Also enable audit logging for that path.
Alyssa Chen: Security side: OK for up to 7 days with reviewer approval. For anything >7d, need manager + security approval. Please open a ticket in infra-ticketing with the vendor name, business justification, and exact TTL. I will mark approval for 5d once ticket exists.
Nora Patel: Who performs rotation/revocation after the TTL? We should decide the owner so we don't leave creds lying around.
Priya Singh: Ops team rotates/revokes. We can script a workflow: when ticket closes, a job calls: `vault lease revoke -prefix secret/data/vendors/partner-x` and then update the S3 ACL to remove the partner principal. I'll attach a checklist in the ticket.
Jamie Lee: Quick note about logs — make sure the partners never see a response with the secret echoed. CI/build logs have leaked before. Add redaction in the pipeline: `set -o pipefail; echo "$API_KEY" | sed 's/.*/****/'` and in Buildkite/CI set SECRET_MASKING=true.
Omar Patel: Good call. Also: should we wrap the key with KMS or HSM before handing it to the partner? What's the difference here?
Priya Singh: For symmetric API keys KMS (customer-managed key) is fine to encrypt at rest. HSM usage is reserved for private keys / signing keys where we need hardware-backed key operations. Wrapping with KMS adds an extra layer: store ciphertext in ticket instead of plain secret. But still give the plaintext to partner over secure channel (eg. 1Password shared item or vendor portal) — do not paste in Slack.
Alyssa Chen: Agreed. Use KMS-encrypted storage + Vault gating. For delivery: use 1Password shared entry or our secure file transfer link. No Slack. Also add this checklist in the ticket: justification, TTL, storage path, delivery method, post-rotation verification.
Jamie Lee: Quick command snippets:

```
# create ephemeral AWS-style creds via Vault (example)
vault write aws/sts/redwood-staging-role ttl=24h
# revoke all leases for the vendor
vault lease revoke -prefix "aws/sts/vendor-partner-x"
```

And for KMS-wrapping (GCP example):

```
echo -n "$API_KEY" | gcloud kms encrypt --keyring=redwood --key=vendor-wrap --plaintext-file=- --ciphertext-file=- | base64 > /tmp/key.cipher
```

Do not commit these to repo.
Omar Patel: I'll open the ticket now (INFRA-2140), include the vendor contact, TTL=120h, delivery via 1Password. @Alyssa Chen can you approve on the ticket?
Alyssa Chen: I'll review INFRA-2140 in ~30m and approve for 5 days. Remember to add the audit log link and the policy path. :thumbsup:
vault-bot: Audit: enabled for secret path `secret/data/vendors/*` (policy=vendor-audit) — logs forwarded to secure-logs.
Omar Patel: Thanks everyone — will not post secrets here. I'll update the ticket once delivery is done.
Priya Singh: One more: add CI static scan to detect accidental AWS key patterns in PRs. `pre-commit` rule + grep check. Saves a headache.
Jamie Lee: +1, added to our infra backlog. :white_check_mark:
